bounds: C/D are proven by the packages' behaviour suites over the sources, not by a dist import: the plugin package's public entry re-exports the plugin contract only, so panel-attention's helpers are not importable from dist. The ADAPTER artifact (A/B) IS the shipped bytes.

THE AUTO-OPEN TRIGGER IS WORKSPACE-SCOPED, not session-scoped: the mpdTeams feed carries no session id and no documented dsh-tui seam exposes the on-screen session to apply-side code. A trigger from another session therefore opens the page, which draws its own 'no team in this session' marker rather than a wrong board.
No real PTY capture in this wave: the change is registration/publication plumbing, not drawing. The DAG visual wave carries the PTY-capture obligation.
dsh-tui 0.16.1's own enable-list behaviour was read from the installed host package (register/dispose/settings-apply), not re-measured on a live boot in this lane.

dockerCiFailure.rootCause: the docker TUI lane seeds its team fixture AFTER the TUI booted (tui-lane.sh: fixture at ~line 510, boot at ~line 402), so the new auto-open opened the MPD sidebar page before the lane's PRE-KEY control capture; docker/lib/tui-panel-body.ts then correctly refused to credit alt+a with the open (controlHits=6).
dockerCiFailure.fix: two changes: (1) the auto-open is now EDGE-triggered (a not-live -> live transition; a boot-time team and any later status change on it open nothing), which is also a real defect fix raised by review; (2) the lane pins the knob OFF in the profile's USER patch layer (`- id: mpd-tui / config: panelAutoOpen: false`) so the lane measures what it claims regardless of when its fixture appears. The knob belongs to a bundle-owned row, so the pin is an id-targeted CONFIG override, never a host-row override.
dockerCiFailure.note: the same edge-trigger also protects the sandbox lane (skills/dsh-qa/scripts/tui-deps-ctrla.ts), which writes its team fixture BEFORE the boot and therefore never auto-opens.

secondCorrection.observed: the first pin attempt made the TUI fail to boot: `pane-boot.txt` on the 2026-10-20 CI run carried `dsh: failed to parse overlay … cordis.patch.yml: YAMLException: end of the stream or a document separator is expected (7:1)` and the lane recorded 8 failures that all read as 'the fixture did not bind'.
secondCorrection.cause: the profile's user layer is ONE YAML document whose stock content is the empty array `[]`; appending a list item after that complete document makes the overlay unparseable. The id-target shape also carries `name` (the loader patch dialect the installer writes).
secondCorrection.fix: the lane deletes the stock `[]` marker line first (so the file stays ONE array document) and appends a full id-target row (`id` + `name` + `config.panelAutoOpen: false`). Both the fixed shape and the negative control were checked with the host's own YAML parser: the fixed file parses to the expected entry; the old append fails with the same class of error the boot pane showed.

codeRabbitFindings.finding: badgePanel conflated an absent host badge member with a callable refusal, so a refusal settled the value and was never retried
codeRabbitFindings.fix: badgePanel now answers boolean | undefined: undefined = no member (settles, cannot change), false = callable refusal (retried on the next state change); index.ts returns undefined when the seam has no badge member. Two new arms pin both paths.

codeRabbitFindings.finding: the initial observe(false) skipped auto-open but did not record that a team already existed, so a later feed event could open the page for a boot-time team
codeRabbitFindings.fix: wasLive tracks the previous pass and the open is now edge-triggered; a new arm fires events over a boot-time team and expects zero opens.

codeRabbitFindings.finding: the feed was resolved once at arm; when the panel seam binds before mpdTeams the surface never subscribes (no badge, no auto-open, silently)
codeRabbitFindings.fix: PanelAttention.resubscribe() re-resolves the feed (releasing the previous subscription) and the plugin calls it from the mpdTeams bind callback; a new arm binds the feed late and proves subscribe + badge + a later appearance.

codeRabbitFindings.finding: the stop() arm proved only that unsubscribe works, because the fake feed always returned a working disposer
codeRabbitFindings.fix: the fake feed gained a noopDisposer option; the arm now leaves the listener attached after stop() and proves the surface's own STOPPED latch suppresses both the badge and the open.
